1.sofaString: 111	Pt, ******* ********, is a 3 year old female with history of restrictive cardiomyopathy referred by ***** ********, ****, Transplant Coordinator, for Heart Transplant Psychosocial Re-check.  Information for this assessment was obtained through an interview with the parents and review of the medical records.  SW spent 45 minutes of face to face time with family.     Living situation:  **, *******, lives with her mother and father in ********, *******.  They reside at **** *** ** *, ********, ** *****. They live in * ****** home with a/c and heat window units, and well water.  They clean their air filter monthly.  There is a filter on the water as well.  There is no smoking in the home.  They have a cat and a dog.      Demographics:  Mother:  ******** ********   DOB:  **/**/****  Phone:  ***-***-****     Father:  ***** ********   DOB:  **/**/****  Employment:  ******'s ***** Tinting  Phone:  ***-***-****     Siblings:  ******* ********, 1 yr     Support systems:  ******** and ***** lean on and depend on each other for support. They also have a close knit family. Most of *****'s family lives in the same immediate area. ******** also has involved family members.   ******* will be starting preschool in a few weeks.  The family has already updated the school regarding her medical condition and needs.      ******* is covered by ********/******** insurance.  She also receives SSI.     Both ******** and ***** have vehicles.  The family lives about 3.5 hours from the hospital. They deny any difficulty getting ******* to appointments.   The family identifies as *******.  They deny any objections to blood products, transfusions, etc.     Course of illness:     ******* was originally seen at ******* in ********* for new onset murmur. She underwent a work-up with EKG and ECHO. EKG showed bilateral atrial enlargement, bilateral ventricular hypertrophy with strain, and T waves were inverted in all leads. ECHO showed bilateral atrial enlargement, abnormal mitral inflow (single inflow wave with loss of a and e pattern), wave reversal seen on pulmonary venous doppler suggesting increased filling pressure, and normal ventricular function. She was diagnosed with hypertrophic restrictive cardiomyopathy and was seen for heart transplant evaluation.  She was doing well at the time and was not listed as a result.  She has become more symptomatic over the past few months.  She is now being reconsidered for active listing on the heart transplant list.     Financial situation:  ******* is covered by ********/******** Medicaid. She receives SSi as well.  The family is supported by dad's employment income as well.  Finances will be a stressor for family but they do have a significant amount of extended family support.               Family History:  Family denies any history with DCF in regards to *******. ******** did have DCF involvement as a child victim. Her mother was the perpetrator but she is no longer involved in the family's life.    Family denies any mental health or substance abuse history.        Family medical history significant for hypertension, high cholesterol, heart failure, COPD, and diabetes in older family members (grandparents, etc).      Adherence:  There are no concerns for adherence noted. *******, ******* does have some difficulty taking medications.       Assessment and recommendations:  Both ******** and ***** verbalize that they are agreeable to proceeding with transplant if indicated. They also seem to have a good grasp on the realities and risks of transplant.    They both seem very bonded with *******.  They appear to be good historians of her medical history, and interactive in her care.             (Low Risk - 1; Moderate Risk - 2; High Risk - 3; Severe Risk - 4)     Home Environment/Transportation -  1     Family Background & Social Support -  1     Financial/Insurance  - 2     Mental Health/Substance Abuse - 1     Involvement with *** Enforcement/Child Protection -  1     Adherence - 1     Understanding of medical situation & transplant process -  1     Health Literacy -  2     Coping Skills - 1     Total:  11  Low     The family scores as low risk in regards to psychosocial contra-indicators to transplant.       The primary concerns are the financial stressors.
